18	E1 [stage S1] Incident ticket INC-4471, checkout on-call (system-record): INC-4471 opened 3 March 11:20 by paging alert checkout_payment_failure_rate (rule: 30-minute failure rate at least 2% AND at least 40 failed attempts). 20	E3 [stage S1] Release notes, checkout-api v4.12 (CHG-2214) (change-record): checkout-api v4.12, deployed 3 March 10:40, CHG-2214, approved by Engineering CAB. 21	E4 [stage S1] Quillmark Payments status page capture and support ticket TS-90412 (vendor-account): Quillmark status page, captured 6 March 08:00: 'All systems operational' for Authorisation API, Search API and Merchant Dashboard on every day from 1 to 6 March; no incidents posted. Please review your integration and confirm you are handling all documented response codes.'

I need a figure for the board pack on Monday, and I expect us to restate the Q1 forecast on the back of it.

In nine of those cases the bank said it had no record of any authorisation attempt at the time of the failure. Agents have been advising customers to try a different card.
24	CATALOGUE (full contents)
25	C1 [stage S1] Canary rollback test results, CHG-2231, 5 March 12:00–18:00 - Checkout platform team (change-record): CHG-2231 canary, 5 March 12:00–18:00. 8 of 16 checkout-api pods rolled back to v4.11; the load balancer split traffic evenly. Gateway connection-pool utilisation peaked at 31% (pool size 64 after v4.12, 50 before). p99 gateway call latency was 430 ms before the release and 410 ms after. Zero socket timeouts and zero connection-refused errors in the period. No autoscaling events.
27	C3 [stage S1] Per-minute payment failure counts, 3–6 March - Checkout analytics (telemetry): Per-minute failed payment attempts, 3–6 March. HTTP 429 responses: 0 on 1–2 March; 4,980–6,310 per day on 3–6 March, all within burst minutes, header X-RateLimit-Scope: credential. Issuer declines steady at 0.3–0.4% of payments. 33	C9 [stage S1] Sample of 50 Customer Care tickets, 3–6 March - Customer Care (customer-account): Random sample of 50 tickets tagged 'payment' from 3–6 March. 44 mention a declined card. 31 customers completed the order on a later retry, 6 said they abandoned, and 7 were unclear. 3 complained of duplicate charges; all were verified as pending authorisations released within 48 hours. 34	C10 [stage S1] Peer review record for the v4.12 gateway client change (PR #1187) - Source control system (document): PR #1187, merged 2 March. Two approvals. 412 unit tests and 38 integration tests passed. Reviewer comment: 'Error mapping simplification loses upstream status detail. Accepted per product request.' Second reviewer: 'Pool sizing fine. Retry policy unchanged: one retry on timeout only, none on HTTP error responses.' No open review threads at merge.
35	C11 [stage S1] Internal audit finding SEC-2291 and remediation correspondence - Internal Audit (document): SEC-2291, raised 9 February: checkout-api debug logs contained partial card numbers (more than first six and last four digits) for about 0.8% of requests, retained for 30 days in the central log store. Remediation deadline 13 March. Audit memo: 'Any regression after remediation must be reported to the acquiring bank within 5 business days.' Status: closed by v4.12 on 3 March, pending audit verification.
36	C12 [stage S1] Gateway TLS certificate, DNS and egress firewall change history, January–March - Platform team (change-record): Quillmark gateway endpoint certificate last rotated 14 January; next rotation due 14 July. No DNS changes for api.quillmark.example in February or March. Egress firewall and NAT rules for checkout-api unchanged since 20 February. No proxy or service-mesh changes in the period. No TLS handshake errors in checkout-api logs, 1–6 March.
37	CANDIDATES
38	H1: A defect in checkout-api v4.12 (the new gateway HTTP client or its connection-pool settings) is causing the rise in payment failures.
39	H2: Quillmark is throttling Fernhollow's shared gateway credential because the finance settlement-reconciliation job's quarter-hourly search bursts push it over its per-credential rate limit, and checkout payment calls are rejected as a result.
40	H3: A real rise in card issuers declining payments (for example tighter issuer fraud rules) is driving the rise in failures.
41	H4: A platform-wide degradation at Quillmark, affecting its merchants generally, is causing the failures.
42	R1: Deployment of checkout-api v4.12 on 3 March at 10:40 -> Rise in checkout payment failure rate from about 0.4% to about 3.7% (causes)
43	R2: settle-recon moved to a 15-minute daytime schedule on the shared credential fernhollow-prod-01 (FIN-CHG-0187) -> Quillmark returning HTTP 429 rate-limit responses to fernhollow-prod-01 (causes)
44	R3: Quillmark returning HTTP 429 rate-limit responses to fernhollow-prod-01 -> Customers seeing 'card declined' failures at checkout (causes)
45	R4: Rise in checkout payment failure rate since 3 March -> 9% week-on-week fall in gross online revenue for the week to 6 March (causes)

47	A2: Revert settle-recon to its nightly schedule (or pause its daytime runs) now, then watch the 429 rate and payment failure rate to confirm recovery, and give the job its own credential before any future daytime schedule.

49	A4: Ask Quillmark for a temporary increase in the rate limit for credential fernhollow-prod-01.

answers.justification: In the C1 canary, v4.11 and v4.12 pods failed at the same rate (3.7% vs 3.6%); C3 shows failure clusters from 09:00, before the 10:40 deploy; and C2 shows no pool saturation, timeouts or latency change.

C4 shows settle-recon search bursts of 360–430/min against a 300/min per-credential limit, with 429s only in burst minutes and scoped to the credential; C5 confirms the schedule change; C3 matches the quarter-hour pattern and shows no clusters during the 13:00–15:00 pause; C1 shows 341 of 351 v4.11 failures were HTTP 429.

C4 shows issuer declines steady at 0.3–0.4%; only 10 of 351 failures in C1 were 402 card declines; C8 shows no change in 3-D Secure or fraud screening; and in E6, banks had no record of the authorisation attempts.
E4 shows a green status page and no platform-wide incidents; the 429s are scoped to Fernhollow's credential (C4) and follow its own job schedule, stopping when the job paused (C3).
Failures began before the deploy (C3), and rolling half the fleet back to v4.11 left the failure rate unchanged (C1), so the timing link in E2 is not causal.

The order of events (C5 effective 3 March, 429s start 09:00 per C4), the mechanism (bursts above the 300/min credential limit), exact minute-level matching (C3, C4) and a natural pause in the 13:00–15:00 window (C3) together establish causation.

C1 shows most failed payments were 429s; E3 shows every non-2xx response is shown to customers as 'Your card was declined'; and E6 shows banks never saw the attempts, consistent with rejection at the gateway.

The failures and the revenue drop overlap in time, but C6 (clearance week as baseline, lower conversion from display traffic, lower average order value) and C9 (most customers completed on retry) point to large confounders, so causation is not established.

C1 shows a rollback does not reduce failures, and per E3 and C11 it would bring back the SEC-2291 card-number logging, triggering a report to the acquiring bank, while a release freeze punishes the wrong team.

C5 says reverting the cron schedule takes effect from the next run, C3 shows failures stop when the job pauses, and the action includes monitoring to confirm recovery plus a fix (a separate credential) for the shared-credential root cause.

The revenue attribution is unestablished: C6's confounders (end of Winter Clearance, lower conversion and order value) and C9's retry successes suggest the payment failures explain only a small part of the 9%, so giving the board this figure and restating the forecast is unjustified now.
Raising the limit would relieve the throttling (C4), but it takes 3–5 business days, costs money, and treats the symptom rather than the internal schedule change (C5) that A2 fixes immediately.

C1, C3, C4 and C5 together identify the shared-credential rate limiting with a confirming natural experiment, which is enough to commit to reverting the settle-recon schedule and declining the rollback.
